parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no border/document friction documented, no facility or custody rule reaching visitors, and gender identity is a protected ground in the goods-and-services, education and health provisions of the 2010 anti-discrimination law; hate-crime and hate-speech enhancements cover gender identity, though prosecutors downgrade charges, a genuine recourse gap. The negatives are societal: a regional review records continued anti-LGBT hate speech and political rhetoric, with a gender-nonconforming public figure facing threats and several physical attacks, and Pride history shows organised rock-throwing met by heavy state protection — the state acting as protector, not threat. These are largely resident/local-sphere and partly dated (2011–2013); no trans visitor-targeted incident appears in a well-documented record, which is a mildly positive signal. Restrictive legal gender recognition is resident-facing and not deducted. Sits above the 0.55 tier (no recurring visitor-facing service denial) and slightly below 0.65 anchors that document working service remedies and convictions.
